market_question: Will New People (NL) gain the most seats in the next Russian parliamentary election?
reasoning: New People (NL) gained only 12 seats in 2021, not the highest net gain (CPRF gained 15). The party is a Kremlin-sanctioned spoiler that could be dissolved, merged, or sidelined before 2026, making a repeat appearance unlikely. In a tightly managed election, the largest seat gain is likely to accrue to United Russia or a newly introduced vehicle, not a struggling opposition-lite party. Even if NL survives, the probability of them achieving the single largest seat increase relative to 2021 is very low.
evidence_points: In the 2021 State Duma election, New People won 12 seats but did not have the largest gain; the Communist Party (CPRF) gained 15 seats.
New People was created as a Kremlin-friendly party to channel protest votes; its future is uncertain given the post-2022 crackdown and talk of mergers or dissolution.
Russian elections are managed; parties that gain the most seats are typically either the ruling United Russia or a newly approved entity, not an existing small party.
sources_consulted: Meduza / Reuters reporting on New People's creation and role
Carnegie Endowment analysis of Russian party system
